description: This entry covers Malabar spinach (bachali, poi), a fast-growing leafy vine grown in kitchen gardens and small plots through the warm, humid months. Leaves and tender shoots are picked every few days, so sprays must be kept to a minimum and waiting periods observed.
npk_split: Apply half the N with all P and K at planting along with well-rotted farmyard manure, and top-dress the remaining N in small doses after each cutting.

Anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
Anthracnose.description: A fungal leaf spot that develops in warm, wet weather and makes the leaves unfit for sale. It starts as water-soaked spots that dry into brown, papery patches.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn tan to brown
Spots enlarge and merge into dead patches
Centres become thin and papery and may fall out
Tiny dark dots in the centre of old spots
Anthracnose.spread: Survives on plant debris and infected planting material and spreads by rain splash and overhead watering.
Anthracnose.action: Pick and destroy spotted leaves, stop overhead watering, and spray copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L only if the spots keep spreading.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: Harvest marketable leaves first and observe the label waiting period before the next picking.

treatment.name: Pseudomonas fluorescens
treatment.notes: Safer option for a leafy crop that is picked often; spray after each cutting in wet weather.

Bacterial spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Bacterial spot.description: A bacterial leaf spot that spreads fast after rain and makes the leaves unmarketable. Antibiotics must not be used; control depends on keeping the leaves dry and on copper sprays.
symptoms: Small water-soaked angular spots, seen best from the underside
Spots turn dark brown to black, often with a yellow halo
Spots merge and the leaf tears
Bacterial spot.spread: Spread by rain splash, overhead watering, and hands and tools when plants are handled wet.
Bacterial spot.action: Remove spotted leaves, keep the foliage dry, and spray copper hydroxide 77 WP 2 g/L if the disease is spreading.

treatment.name: Copper hydroxide 77 WP
treatment.notes: Harvest marketable leaves first and observe the label waiting period before the next picking.

treatment.name: Dry-leaf handling
treatment.notes: Water at the base, train vines on a trellis and do not pick or prune when leaves are wet.

Downy mildew.name: Downy Mildew
Downy mildew.description: A leaf disease of cool, humid weather that shows as yellow patches on top of the leaf with downy growth underneath. Affected leaves curl, turn brown and cannot be sold.
symptoms: Pale yellow irregular patches on the upper leaf surface
Grey to purplish downy growth on the underside below the patches
Downy mildew.spread: Spores spread by wind and water splash when leaves stay wet for long periods in cool, humid weather.
Downy mildew.action: Remove affected leaves, train the vines on a trellis for airflow, water at the base in the morning, and spray copper oxychloride 50 WP 3 g/L only if it keeps spreading.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: Harvest marketable leaves first and observe the label waiting period before the next picking.

treatment.name: Spacing and airflow
treatment.notes: Avoid crowded planting and overhead watering in the evening.

Insect damage.name: Insect Damage
Insect damage.cause: Chewing or sucking insects of unspecified species (leaf-eating caterpillars, beetles, leaf miners, aphids)
Insect damage.description: Leaf injury caused by insects; the photo shows the damage but not which insect did it. Check the plant to see what is feeding before choosing a control, and prefer hand-picking and neem on this frequently picked leafy crop.
symptoms: White winding mines inside the leaf
Curled tender leaves with clusters of small insects
Insect damage.spread: Adult insects fly in from nearby crops and weeds and multiply quickly in warm weather.
Insect damage.action: Hand-pick caterpillars and damaged leaves, and spray neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L in the evening if damage continues.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: Wash harvested leaves well; avoid synthetic insecticides on a crop picked every few days.

treatment.name: Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki
treatment.notes: Only if caterpillars are found feeding; spray in the evening.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or nutrient problem. Keep up regular picking and balanced nutrition.
symptoms: No spots, holes, mould or yellow patches
healthy.action: Continue regular picking and check the leaf undersides every week.
